newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan security battle youths south of Mombasa. [CORRECTED 10:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Kenyan security battle youths south of Mombasa. [CORRECTED 10:00 GMT]

text.p: Kenyan police and the elite paramilitary General Service Unit (GSU) battled armed youths south of the port city of Mombasa on Friday, two days after attackers killed at least 13 people during a raid, witnesses said. (Corrects date of earlier incident)
"GSU and regular police are battling youths in Ngombeni," a witness told Reuters at Ukunda, on Kenya's lush southcoast.
Police reinforcements and the army were being sent in, witnesses and security officials told Reuters.
The fighting in Ngombeni, 10 km (six miles) south of Mombasa, cut off the main road to Tanzania and all vehicles were being turned back.

Police launched an operation early on Friday to flush out suspected criminals who attacked two police stations and villagers at Likoni in Mombasa on Wednesday night, killing 13 people -- including six police officers.

Witnesses said people were fleeing the Likoni area on Friday and police and the GSU had found some 15 youths, some of them with gunshot wounds, while combing adjacent areas. The youths also had guns, suspected to have been looted from police.
